title: Unit 42 describes Com-affiliated vishing campaigns stealing data from financial, healthcare and legal firms
date_note: Date of Unit 42's report; the activity it describes runs since August 2026.
place: United States (report's most-affected country; no single victim location)
geo_basis: country named by the report as mainly affected
summary: Unit 42 attributes vishing-led data theft and extortion since August 2026 to Com-affiliated actors, mostly against financial services, healthcare and legal organisations in the U.S., UK and Australia. Callers pose as IT staff and send victims to phishing pages that relay credentials and MFA approvals in real time; attackers enrol their own MFA devices within minutes of authenticating. Unit 42 says they occasionally exfiltrated tens of millions of CRM and recruiting records.
plain: Palo Alto's Unit 42 says criminals phone staff pretending to be IT help desks, trick them past multi-factor login, then steal data and demand payment.
exec: Help-desk phone scams are defeating MFA at financial, healthcare and legal firms, leading to large data theft and extortion.
action: Per Unit 42: tighten help desk verification, move to phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/passkeys), use browser extension allowlists, gain visibility into identity actions and alert on unauthorized data exports.
impact: Unit 42 says some intrusions exfiltrated tens of millions of CRM and recruiting records; no victims are named.

validation.note: Vendor research report by Unit 42 (primary); no second publisher read.
